As noted above, there is no widely accepted definition of mass shootings.
People use either broad or restrictive definitions of mass shootings to reinforce their stance on gun control.
After the 2012 Sandy Hook school shooting, Congress defined "mass killings" as three or more homicides in a single incident.
The definition was intended to clarify when the U.S. Attorney General could assist state and local authorities in investigations of violent acts and shootings in places of public use.
